steps.html: In this tutorial, you will learn some basic pool concepts and terminology. You will learn what it means to hit the ball full and to cut the ball. You'll learn what it means to undercut and overcut.
The most basic skill in pool is to strike the white cue ball with a cue and drive an object ball (9-ball in this case) into a pocket.

If the cue ball and object ball are perfectly lined up with the pocket, you can make the ball simply by aiming directly at the center of the object ball. this is called a full hit.

With a full hit the cue ball hits the object ball head-on and the object ball will travel along the same line after the collision.
Watch this demonstration of a full hit.

In most cases, the balls are not lined up perfectly, and you need to send the object ball a bit to to one side or another.
  • If the cue ball strikes the object ball to the right of center, the object ball will go to the left.
  • If the cue ball strikes the object ball to the left of center, the object ball will go to the right.
This is called a cut shot.
In this case, we need to cut the 9-ball to the left, so we'll aim the cue ball a bit to the right of the center of the object ball.  Here's a demonstration.
If you hit the object too far off-center, the object ball will deflect too much. This is called an overcut.
If you don't hit the object off-center enough, the object ball won't deflect enough. This is called an undercut.
It takes judgment and practice to learn just how far off-center the cue ball must strike the object ball for a given shot. MillionBalls helps you learn to visualize shots correctly.

Review

In this tutorial you learned the concept of a basic cut shot.
  • To send the object ball to the left, the cue ball must strike the object ball to the right of center
  • To send the object ball to the right, the cue ball must strike the object ball to the left of center
  • If the object ball deflects too much, this is an overcut and you correct by aiming closer to the center of the object ball
  • If the object ball doesn't deflect enough, this is an undercut and you correct by aiming further from the center of the object ball

You will learn the controls in the next tutorial.
